topics.label: Lecture overview and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture themes, lecturer background, and learning objectives regarding environmental carcinogens and cancer development.

topics.label: Conceptual frameworks and population patterns of cancer causation
topics.groupedBecause: They introduce fundamental concepts in cancer etiology, comparing intrinsic biological processes, environmental exposures, and global epidemiological variations.

topics.label: Infectious pathogens and oncogenic mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: They focus on biological pathogens linked to cancer and examine the cooperative role of Epstein-Barr virus and malaria in Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Aflatoxin metabolism and DNA adduct formation
topics.groupedBecause: It describes how dietary aflatoxin is converted by liver enzymes into a reactive epoxide that forms mutagenic DNA adducts.

topics.label: UV radiation and thymine dimer formation
topics.groupedBecause: It examines the mechanism by which physical ultraviolet radiation damages DNA through the formation of pyrimidine dimers.

topics.label: Metabolic activation and mechanisms of chemical carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: They detail the metabolic pathways and biochemical mechanisms through which environmental chemical compounds become active mutagens in host tissues.

topics.label: Tumor promotion and the two-stage carcinogenesis model
topics.groupedBecause: They explain non-mutagenic mechanisms of carcinogenesis where chronic inflammation and promotional signaling stimulate the proliferation of initiated cells.

topics.label: Host tissue proliferation and developmental susceptibility to carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: It explores how the developmental timing and active proliferative state of specific tissues alter vulnerability to carcinogen exposure.

topics.label: Mutational signatures derived from whole-genome sequencing
topics.groupedBecause: It describes how high-throughput genomic sequencing identifies characteristic mutation patterns left by distinct carcinogens.

topics.label: Epidemiological cohorts, biobanks, and exposure biomarkers
topics.groupedBecause: It covers human population-level methodologies, biobank resources, and urinary biomarkers used to link exposures to cancer development.

topics.label: In vivo animal bioassays and dose-response considerations
topics.groupedBecause: It examines the experimental use, limitations, and dosage parameters of whole-animal rodent bioassays in assessing carcinogenicity.

topics.label: In vitro mutagenicity testing and carcinogen risk evaluation
topics.groupedBecause: It discusses the bacterial Ames test for mutagen screening and reviews how societal risk-benefit assessments apply to carcinogens.
